protocol.instrument_name: Enhanced Access Community Pharmacy Pilot - Participation requirements
protocol.effective_date: Not printed; copyright line reads '© Department of Health 2026'
protocol.legal_basis: Not stated in this document; no Act, regulation, schedule provision or SASA is cited. The document sets out mandatory participation requirements for the Enhanced Access Community Pharmacy Pilot (EACPP).
protocol.supervision_model: Not stated in this document; the requirements mandate that participating pharmacists provide services 'in accordance with the relevant EACPP Clinical Practice Guideline or Protocol at a participating pharmacy' and use 'an approved EACPP Clinical Information System', and that services are provided under the EACPP rules and conditions in the EACPP Handbook (p.1).
protocol.scope_summary: SUPPORTING / ADMINISTRATIVE DOCUMENT, NOT A CLINICAL PRESCRIBING PROTOCOL: mandatory participation requirements for participating pharmacists (6 requirements, pages 1-2) and participating pharmacies (7 requirements, pages 2-3) under the WA Enhanced Access Community Pharmacy Pilot, plus a requirement to apply separately. It contains registration, insurance, training, accreditation, infrastructure and database-listing conditions only - no patient eligibility criteria, no medicines, no doses, no assessment pathway and no red-flag/referral triggers, which are genuinely absent.

inclusion.text: The pharmacist must hold general registration with the Pharmacy Board of Australia, with no conditions on practice.
The pharmacist must hold appropriate professional indemnity insurance to cover the services provided as part of the EACPP.
The pharmacist must hold, for the duration of the EACPP, certification for First Aid and CPR.

The pharmacist must demonstrate successful completion of an approved training program that covers the knowledge and skills required to deliver EACPP services. An approved training program must be: a. Accredited by the Australian Pharmacy Council (APC) in accordance with the Accreditation Standards for Pharmacist Prescriber education programs. b. Recognised as an Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) Level 8 Graduate Certificate. c. Assessed and approved by the Department of Health (the department) and published on the EACPP website.

The pharmacist must agree to the rules and conditions set out in the EACPP Handbook, including: a. Providing services in accordance with the relevant EACPP Clinical Practice Guideline or Protocol at a participating pharmacy. b. Using an approved EACPP Clinical Information System to record clinical consultations and collect data for the evaluation of the EACPP. c. Participation in other activities that are required to enable quality and safety monitoring and evaluation of the EACPP.
The pharmacist must agree to their full name and Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency registration number appearing in the EACPP participating pharmacist database.

The pharmacy be accredited against, or actively progressing towards accreditation against the AS85000:2024 Australian Community Pharmacy Standard through an approved pharmacy or primary care accreditation program, such as the Quality and Safety Pharmacy Program (QSPP). Participating pharmacies are to hold or actively progress towards QSPP accreditation that includes Full Scope of Practice certification (or equivalent): Pharmacies currently holding Quality Care Pharmacy Program (QCPP) accreditation will transition to QSPP on 1 October 2026: QSPP has advised that these pharmacies that wish to be considered for EACPP must apply for a QSPP Expansion of Service, Full Scope of Practice assessment; these pharmacies must submit the QSPP Accreditation Certificate that includes Full Scope of Practice certification as part of their EACPP application; QSPP has advised that where a QSPP accredited pharmacy is found to have been offering or advertising a service which is not within the service level for which they are QSPP accredited, a sanction may be issued by QSPP; please refer to the QSPP Knowledge Hub (member log-in required) for more information. Pharmacies with no current accreditation must attain a QSPP Accreditation Certificate that includes Full Scope of Practice certification (or equivalent) by 30 June 2027.
The pharmacy owner must demonstrate compliance with appropriate infrastructure requirements as set out in the EACPP Handbook.
The pharmacy must have access to an approved EACPP Clinical Information System software to record clinical consultations and collect data for the evaluation of the EACPP.
The pharmacy owner must hold, for the duration of the EACPP, professional indemnity insurance that explicitly covers the pharmacy's involvement in the EACPP.
The pharmacy owner must provide access for participating pharmacists to the required resources and reference materials.
The pharmacy owner must provide access for participating pharmacists to the current online version of the Therapeutic Guidelines.
The pharmacy owner must agree to their pharmacy information appearing in the EACPP participating pharmacy premises database and Find a Pharmacy website.
Pharmacists and pharmacies must apply separately to participate in the EACPP. Application forms for EACPP participation are available on the EACPP website.

red_flags.trigger_text: QSPP has advised that where a QSPP accredited pharmacy is found to have been offering or advertising a service which is not within the service level for which they are QSPP accredited, a sanction may be issued by QSPP.

open_questions.topic: This is an administrative participation-requirements document, not a clinical prescribing protocol
open_questions.observed: The document sets out 'Requirements for participating pharmacists' (items 1-6, pages 1-2), 'Requirements for participating pharmacies' (items 1-7, pages 2-3), a requirement to apply separately, and a version table (1.0 First version; 1.1 Revised version, updated QSPP requirements). It contains no patient eligibility criteria, no medicines or doses, no assessment/diagnosis pathway, no referral or escalation triggers and no clinical content.
open_questions.why_unclear: Per the extraction spec's NON-PROTOCOL DOCUMENTS rule, clinical arrays (diagnosis_pathways, treatments, red_flags, review_followup) are left empty because the document genuinely has none; the administrative requirements are captured as eligibility criteria with provenance instead of being fabricated into clinical criteria.

open_questions.topic: No patient-facing exclusion criteria or clinical referral/escalation triggers are printed
open_questions.observed: All requirements are stated positively as conditions that must be met ('must hold', 'must have access', 'must agree'); the document contains no patient-facing exclusion criteria and no clinical referral or urgency wording. The single escalation/consequence clause is administrative: a QSPP sanction where a pharmacy offers or advertises a service outside its accredited service level (p.2).
open_questions.why_unclear: exclusion, referral and review_followup are empty because the document genuinely has none; RF-1 captures the only trigger wording present (its action is mapped to NOT_ELIGIBLE because the spec's action enum has no SANCTION value).

open_questions.observed: The document sets pharmacist and pharmacy conditions only; no patient or practitioner age limit appears on any of the 3 pages.
open_questions.why_unclear: age_bounds is null/null with provenance to the eligibility (participation requirements) section.

open_questions.topic: Referenced instruments are not included with this document
open_questions.observed: The requirements depend on the EACPP Handbook (rules, conditions and infrastructure requirements), the list of approved EACPP Clinical Information Systems, EACPP Clinical Practice Guidelines/Protocols, the EACPP website list of approved training programs, and the application forms - none of which are reproduced in this document.
open_questions.why_unclear: Those documents cannot be transcribed from this file; their content is recorded here as an open item rather than inferred.

open_questions.topic: Public disclosure of practitioner and pharmacy details is required, not a notifiable-condition requirement
open_questions.observed: The pharmacist's full name and AHPRA registration number must appear in the EACPP participating pharmacist database, and pharmacy information must appear in the EACPP participating pharmacy premises database and Find a Pharmacy website. No notifiable condition, GP notification or AIR notification is mentioned.
open_questions.why_unclear: notifiable.required is null because the document is silent on statutory notification; the database/website publication obligations are captured as eligibility criteria INC-6 and INC-13.

open_questions.topic: No effective date printed beyond copyright year
open_questions.observed: The version table lists '1.0 First version' and '1.1 Revised version, updated QSPP requirements' with no dates; the only date-style text on the document is '© Department of Health 2026'.
open_questions.why_unclear: effective_date cannot be populated from the document beyond the copyright year note.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the QSPP/QCPP transition dates and accreditation deadlines are current and in force at go-live: QCPP-accredited pharmacies transition to QSPP on 1 October 2026 and must apply for a QSPP Expansion of Service, Full Scope of Practice assessment; pharmacies with no current accreditation must attain a QSPP Accreditation Certificate that includes Full Scope of Practice certification (or equivalent) by 30 June 2027.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: These are dated, jurisdiction-specific accreditation conditions in a pilot document (version 1.1 'updated QSPP requirements'); they must be verified against the current QSPP/department position before the module relies on them.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the specific approved training program(s) published on the EACPP website (APC-accredited, AQF Level 8 Graduate Certificate) that satisfy requirement 4.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The document defines what an approved program must be but does not name any course; go-live eligibility checks need the actual approved list.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the contents of the EACPP Handbook rules/conditions and infrastructure requirements (referenced in requirements 5 and 2) and the list of approved EACPP Clinical Information Systems.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Two mandatory requirements are defined purely by reference to documents not supplied; local confirmation is needed before treating them as evaluable checks.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm that version 1.1 (Revised version, updated QSPP requirements) is the current controlled version of this document with the Department of Health, and obtain its issue/effective date.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The version table prints version numbers with no dates, so effective_date cannot be established from the document alone.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm how participation compliance is monitored after application (that requirements 'remain in place for the duration' is asserted in the companion application information pack, not in this document) and which party verifies ongoing pharmacist/pharmacy compliance.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: This document states the requirements but not the verification or sanction process (other than a QSPP sanction for accreditation breaches), which must be confirmed for local operating procedures.
